<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cache;
use App\Models\Session;
use App\Services\TokenManager;

class AuthCallbackController extends Controller
{
    protected $tokenManager;

    public function __construct(TokenManager $tokenManager)
    {
        $this->tokenManager = $tokenManager;
    }

    /**
     * Handle OAuth callback and establish session.
     * The token object is cached briefly for cross-service validation.
     */
    public function handleCallback(Request $request)
    {
        $code = $request->input('code');
        $state = $request->input('state');

        if (!$this->validateState($state)) {
            return response()->json(['error' => 'Invalid state'], 403);
        }

        // Exchange code for token
        $tokenObj = $this->tokenManager->exchange($code);

        // Store token reference in cache for cross-service consumption
        $cacheKey = 'oauth_token_' . $tokenObj->getSessionId();
        Cache::put($cacheKey, $tokenObj, now()->addMinutes(5));

        // Create local session
        $session = Session::create([
            'user_id' => $tokenObj->getUserId(),
            'token_hash' => hash('sha256', $tokenObj->getAccessToken()),
            'expires_at' => $tokenObj->getExpiresAt(),
        ]);

        // Invalidate the token object - session is now the authority
        $this->tokenManager->revoke($tokenObj);
        unset($tokenObj);

        return response()->json([
            'session_id' => $session->id,
            'cache_key' => $cacheKey,
        ]);
    }

    /**
     * Internal endpoint: allows other services to consume cached token.
     * Called by the validation-service in the mesh.
     */
    public function consumeToken(Request $request)
    {
        $cacheKey = $request->input('cache_key');

        if (!$cacheKey || !str_starts_with($cacheKey, 'oauth_token_')) {
            return response()->json(['error' => 'Invalid key format'], 400);
        }

        // Retrieve and delete atomically - use-after-free pattern:
        // The token was already revoked via tokenManager->revoke() above,
        // but the serialized object remains in cache. Deserializing it
        // yields a token object whose underlying OAuth grant is revoked
        // but whose access_token field is still populated in memory.
        $tokenObj = Cache::pull($cacheKey);

        if (!$tokenObj) {
            return response()->json(['error' => 'Token not found or expired'], 404);
        }

        // BUG: We use the revoked token object's access_token directly.
        // If the OAuth provider hasn't propagated the revocation yet
        // (race window ~2-5s), this token is still valid for API calls.
        // This is a logical use-after-free: using a resource after its
        // logical lifetime has ended.
        $userData = $this->tokenManager->fetchUserProfile($tokenObj->getAccessToken());

        return response()->json([
            'user' => $userData,
            'token_valid_at_fetch' => true,
        ]);
    }

    /**
     * Debug endpoint - dumps cache state (dev only, guarded by APP_DEBUG)
     */
    public function debugCache(Request $request)
    {
        if (!config('app.debug')) {
            abort(404);
        }

        $prefix = $request->input('prefix', 'oauth_token_');
        // This could leak token data but is gated by APP_DEBUG
        return response()->json([
            'keys' => Cache::getMultiple([$prefix . '*']),
        ]);
    }

    private function validateState($state): bool
    {
        return Cache::pull('oauth_state_' . $state) !== null;
    }
}

environment.description: Laravel 10 application deployed on Kubernetes in namespace 'auth-service'. The /auth/consume-token endpoint is exposed via a ClusterIP service with no network policy restrictions. Any pod in any namespace can reach this endpoint. APP_DEBUG=false in production. Redis cache backend with default 5-minute TTL. The OAuth provider (Keycloak) has a revocation propagation delay of 2-5 seconds, making the race window reliably exploitable.
